courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to Theatre
courses.description: An introduction to the art and concepts of theatre through a study of modern and historical theories of dramatic structure, playwriting, directing, design, and acting. Attendance of live theatre required. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre and Cultural Diversity
courses.description: Through lectures, readings, documentaries, and films, the class will illustrate the contributions of diverse cultures to the fabric of American Theatre and entertainment. Focus will be upon the influence of Latino American, Asian American, African American cultures, LGBTQ Americans and the under recognized influence of women playwrights. The class will also present and illustrate alternative theatre viewpoints from political and experimental perspectives. The student will be asked to discuss, react and compare aspects of these diverse theatres/genres, including costume, scenic, lighting and make-up design, and acting style. CSU

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre History 1
courses.description: This course explores the history of theatre from its origins through the 17th Century. The history and development of theatre and drama are studied in relationship to cultural, political and social conditions of the time. Plays are read for analysis of structure, plot, character and historical relevance. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Stage Management
courses.description: Exploration of the study and practical application practices of the stage manager as they pertain to the theatrical production process. Emphasis is placed on the duties, responsibilities, and procedures from pre-production to post-production. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting Fundamentals
courses.description: A study of acting involving the development of acting techniques, styles, and disciplines. Provides theory and practical experience with varied characterizations. Emphasizes individual growth and acquired skills necessary to the acting craft. A combination of Theatre Arts 110, 111, and 118 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Intermediate Acting
courses.description: Further study in the art of acting for the stage, investigating in-depth character study, role portrayal, special problems, and personal technique. Acting skills developed through use of exercises, monologues, and scenes from contemporary theatre. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting for the Camera
courses.description: Techniques and disciplines of acting as applied to film and television production. Opportunity to practice and perform with emphasis on developing talents and skills required in acting for the screen (Same as DM 142). (Same as Digital Media 142). A combination of Digital Media 142, Theatre Arts 113, and 256 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting for the Camera II
courses.description: An intermediate and immersive on-camera experience in which the student will have opportunities to practice skills and techniques in several styles of camera production: movie/TV narrative drama, comedy, and reality TV. The material from these performances is edited, screened, and discussed. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to Technical Theatre
courses.description: A project-based course involving the study and execution of technical theater principles. Students will learn the theatrical design and technical practices that apply to scenery, lighting, sound, costumes, make up, properties, and scene painting. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Musical Theatre History
courses.description: This course explores the history of the uniquely American art form that is musical theatre from its early development in the colonial period to the present time. Emphasis will be placed on the chronological examination of various musical theatre productions. Students will learn how the composers, librettists, lyricists, choreographers, directors, and designers contributed to the formation and the popularity of musical theatre as it exists today. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to Drama and Acting
courses.description: An introduction to acting and dramatic literature that includes analysis of plays, dramatic structure, and performance criticism. This course explores the history and development of acting styles and methodologies specific to the major historical periods of drama in which they were created. Intended to enhance imagination and creativity and emphasize intellectual growth through the exploration of the cultural significance of drama and performance. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to Sound Design
courses.description: A study of sound design principles and practices and the sound technology used to bring sound to the stage and the concert hall. Project-based learning provides the student with an introduction to audio equipment and an understanding of the craft and process of sound design. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to Lighting Design
courses.description: An overview of the methods and techniques of the lighting designer. The course includes training in the creative concepts of design and the practical operation of the equipment used to execute the design. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Stagecraft
courses.description: An introduction to technical theatre and the creation of scenic elements including design concepts, painting techniques, set construction, set movement, prop construction, backstage organization, and stage management. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Stage Makeup
courses.description: Basic techniques and artistry of stage makeup and its relation to the total production. Covers history, aesthetics and design theory, color theory, materials, and application procedures for varied characterizations. Practical application of learned skills are applied to departmental productions. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Lighting Fundamentals
courses.description: Theory and practices of lighting including control systems and instruments as well as the techniques for proper installation, operation, maintenance, and safety. (Same as Digital Media 260). CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Technical Production
courses.description: Instruction and practical experience in backstage production responsibilities including stage management, scenery construction, properties, costuming, lighting, sound, and running crews. May be repeated. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to Stage Costume
courses.description: Students will study costume history, design, and basic construction techniques as an introduction to basic theatrical costuming. Fabrics and their various uses will be investigated. (Same as Fashion Design & Merchandising 136). CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Costume Design and Construction
courses.description: Explores the many aspects of costume design, including the breakdown of a script, artistic rendering of the literature, development of themes and design concepts, research sources, examination of the social and economic mores that govern dress, and the history of dress. Students will analyze, research, and design two plays to present to the class. The course will include film and theatre industry standards in the area of costume design. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Costume Periods and Styles
courses.description: A study of the changes in dress from ancient times to the present. Social and political influences, as well as the historical accuracy of period dress, are considered relative to the practical needs of costuming for stage, film, and television. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre Performance
courses.description: An introduction to theatre performance emphasizing acting technique, theatre vocabulary, and creative individual expression. Students learn the process of presenting a role on stage. Prepares the student for Theatre Performance 140B. All actors must audition and be cast prior to enrolling. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre Performance II
courses.description: Continued study in theatre performance emphasizing acting technique, theatre vocabulary, and creative individual expression. Students perfect the process of presenting a role on stage. Theatre Arts 140B is a continuation and refinement of the work begun during Theatre Arts 140A. All actors must audition and be cast prior to enrolling. CSU/UC

courses.description: Provides the continuing theatre performance student opportunity to concentrate on more advanced acting methods and development of technique. Emphasizes the development of the individual actor's performance style connecting the voice and body with the emotional life of a character. All actors must audition and be cast prior to enrolling. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Rehearsal and Performance in Production
courses.description: Practical experience in performance production culminating in a series of public performances. All actors must audition and be cast prior to enrolling. May be repeated. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Technical Theatre in Production
courses.description: Students will gain practical experience in the application of production responsibilities in any of the following: stage management, scenery construction, properties, costuming, lighting, or sound. This course culminates into a series of public performances. All student technicians must obtain instructor approval prior to enrolling. May be repeated. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Showcase I
courses.description: An introduction to theatre performance emphasizing acting technique, theatre vocabulary, and creative individual expression. Students learn the process of presenting a role on stage. Prepares the student for Showcase II. A combination of Theatre Arts 151, 171, 172, and 173 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Technical Showcase Production
courses.description: Application of scenic, costume, lighting, or audio crafts for a live performance. This course culminates in a series of public performances. CSU

courses.subject: THEA

May be repeated. A combination of THEA 154 and THEA 155 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Children's Theatre Ensemble
courses.description: Intensive rehearsal and performance experience leading to an extended-run Children's Theatre production utilizing playscripts written for young audiences. May be repeated. A combination of THEA 154 and THEA 155 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.title: Formerly: Introduction to Entertainment Lighting
courses.description: This course explores stage lighting, projection, lighting control systems, optical systems, color theory, and current lighting graphic standards as they apply to stage, film, and video. Students demonstrate their skills through projects, programming, and rigging. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Fundamentals of Programming
courses.description: Develop the programming skills to complete a show set up, control fixture characteristics, create and record cues, and transfer between programming and show control. Emphasis will be placed on developing speed and accuracy in these basic skills. CSU

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Work Experience - Theatre
courses.description: This work experience course of supervised employment is designed to assist students to acquire desirable work habits, attitudes and skills in a field related to the students' major so as to enable them to become productive employees. Students may earn a maximum of 14 units of credit for work experience. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. Open Entry/Open Exit. CSU

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Principles of Playwriting
courses.description: An introduction to the elements of writing a play for the stage emphasizing dramatic structure, dramatic action, relationship between dialogue and action, setting, theme and point of view. Students will be assigned writing exercises that culminate in a one-act play. Same as ENG 177, Principles of Playwriting. A combination of Theatre Arts 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 186, and 190 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Musical Theatre Techniques
courses.description: This course explores the development of the beginning fundamentals of acting, singing and movement for musical theatre through exercises, auditions, solo and group performances. A combination of Theatre Arts 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 186, and 190 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Musical Theatre Workshop
courses.description: Development and exploration of musical theatre skills. Students will become proficient musical theatre artists through theatrical exercises, audition and dance techniques and solo and group performances. A combination of Theatre Arts 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 186, and 190 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Intermediate Musical Theatre Techniques
courses.description: This course explores intermediate level techniques of acting, singing and movement for musical theatre through theatrical exercises, auditions, solo and group performances. A combination of Theatre Arts 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 186, and 190 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Intermediate Musical Theatre Workshop
courses.description: Intermediate level development and exploration of musical theatre skills. Students will become proficient musical theatre artists through theatrical exercises, audition and dance techniques and solo and group performances. A combination of Theatre Arts 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 186, and 190 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Voice for the Actor
courses.description: An academic study and practical application of the efficient and effective use of the speaking voice, particularly in meeting the unique demands of acting for the stage. Focus will be placed on exercises designed to identify and correct breathing problems, diction problems, and to create conscious control of speech function. A combination of Theatre Arts 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 186, and 190 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Improvisation for Stage and Screen
courses.description: Exploration of the principles and techniques of improvisational acting designed to increase the actor's creativity, problem solving, and performance skills. This course also develops student awareness of the importance of the cooperative dynamics of theatre, television and film. A combination of Theatre Arts 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 186, and 190 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Advanced Theatre Production
courses.description: Practical experience performing an advanced level role in a series of public performances. May be repeated. CSU/UC

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
